main_body: A wooden rack base (rows 26-46) holding three upright spears with metal tips; the base is drawn as a stacked wooden box with horizontal bands and slats
top_band: none. At the top of the base (row 26) there is a dark outline, then a 1-row light edge (row 27, #d59147) and a 2-row mid band (rows 28-29). Together they are 3 rows with no real step and no horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The rack base is a flat front elevation. Below the dark outline at row 26 comes a 1-row light line (row 27) and a 2-row mid band (rows 28-29), which stays in the same tone family as the front below it. The lower section repeats the same pattern at rows 41-45, with horizontal planks and bands. Nothing reads as a top surface of 3 or more rows. The base is just stacked front-facing bands, so no horizontal surface of the base is visible from above. The spears are vertical poles with no beam tops. This is a front elevation, and the contract for a frame requires its beams and base to show top faces.

style.evidence: The candidate has 13 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 17-20 and 38-40 colours in the references, so it is much lower in density. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which fits the Beodeul approach. The wood has about 4 steps and the spear poles are flat vertical strips with little grain. The steel tips are small, with about 3 tones. The base has some banding and highlight lines but little texture, and it is thinner than the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, but the piece is simple and shallow next to the stall and the well.
